patchouli.mam.verdant_path.landing: The living world speaks in the language of flowers. This tome is your guide to the Verdant Path — a school of magic drawn from the mana of the earth, the light of the divine, and the patience of those who tend to growing things.
patchouli.mam.verdant_path.category.intr: Begin your journey along the Verdant Path.
patchouli.mam.verdant_path.category.flow: The world blooms with mystical color. Learn to gather petals, cultivate tall flowers, and harness their transformative power.
patchouli.mam.verdant_path.category.mana: The lifeblood of the Verdant Path flows through mana — drawn from the earth by mystical flowers and gathered in pools of living stone.
The Verdant Path is a school of nature magic drawn from the mana of living flowers. Rather than machines or artifice, practitioners of this art tend gardens, grow rare blooms, and channel the quiet power of the natural world.

Begin by finding $(thing)Mystical Flowers$(). They grow wild in sixteen colors — each one a trace of the divine-natural. Gather $(thing)Petals$(), transmute stone into $(thing)Living Rock$(), and tend your first $(thing)Mana Pool$(). The path reveals itself through patient tending.
patchouli.mam.verdant_path.page.mystical: $(thing)Mystical Flowers$() are the foundation of the Verdant Path. They bloom across the world in sixteen colors, each holding a trace of divine-natural power. Break one to collect a $(thing)Petal$() — or craft a flower into four petals at any crafting table.

Applying $(thing)Bone Meal$() to a short Mystical Flower causes it to grow into a tall two-block variant. Tall flowers drop two petals when broken — making them more efficient for petal farming. Right-clicking a petal on dirt plants a hidden $(thing)Buried Petal$() that grows into a flower over time.
patchouli.mam.verdant_path.page.floral_p: $(thing)Floral Powder$() is a scattering of mystical essence. Throw it onto the ground and a burst of $(thing)Mystical Flowers$() will bloom around the impact point in a random assortment of colors — useful for quickly seeding a flower garden without hunting each color individually.
patchouli.mam.verdant_path.page.pure_dai: The $(thing)Pure Daisy$() is a sacred flower of transformation. Placed among ordinary stone, it slowly purifies each adjacent block into $(thing)Living Rock$() — the foundation material of all Verdant Path crafting. Place it near any $(thing)log$() and it will transmute the wood into $(thing)Livingwood Log$() instead.

Each conversion takes about ten seconds. The daisy works on all eight horizontally adjacent blocks one at a time. It does not consume itself — leave it in place and it will keep working as long as there are valid blocks beside it.
patchouli.mam.verdant_path.page.solarbud: The $(thing)Solarbud$() turns to face the sun. Quiet, patient, and perfectly content to stand in a garden and drink in light — it asks nothing of you and gives steadily in return.$(br2)Place it within six blocks of a $(thing)Mana Pool$() and it will begin filling the pool with passive mana as long as the sky above it is clear and the sun is up.

The Solarbud generates $(thing)one mana per tick$() during daylight. Night, cave ceilings, and dense canopies will pause it. It holds up to 900 mana in its stem before pushing the next batch into the nearest pool within six blocks.
patchouli.mam.verdant_path.page.emberwor: The $(thing)Emberwort$() carries a faint warmth even in total darkness. Unlike other flowers, it does not wait for sun or rain — it waits for offerings. Drop any $(thing)furnace fuel$() within three blocks and it will pull the item close and begin to burn.$(br2)Mana rises from the heat.

Coal, charcoal, wood, blaze rods — anything that fuels a furnace will work. The Emberwort consumes one item at a time and generates $(thing)three mana every two ticks$() while burning. It holds up to 300 mana before pushing to a nearby pool.
patchouli.mam.verdant_path.page.dewpetal: The $(thing)Dewpetal$() drinks. Rain, mist, the slow seep of a brook — it does not distinguish. Place it outdoors and it will generate mana whenever it rains. Place it against a $(thing)water source$() and it will generate constantly, regardless of weather.$(br2)Patient. Reliable. Quiet.

The Dewpetal generates $(thing)one mana every two ticks$() when active. A single adjacent water source block provides permanent activation without needing rain. It holds up to 900 mana before pushing to a pool within six blocks.
patchouli.mam.verdant_path.page.mana_poo: The $(thing)Mana Pool$() is a basin carved from $(thing)Living Rock$() that holds up to one million units of mana. Mystical flowers planted nearby will automatically push their generated mana into the nearest pool within six blocks — no wiring required.
Craft a Mana Pool with eight pieces of Living Rock arranged in a U-shape.
A $(thing)Redstone Comparator$() placed next to a Mana Pool outputs a signal proportional to how full the pool is — 0 when empty, up to 15 when completely full. Use this to build mana-aware circuits.
patchouli.mam.verdant_path.page.apotheca: The $(thing)Apothecary$() is the primary crafting station of the Verdant Path. Fill it with water using a bucket, then throw $(thing)Mystical Petals$() into the basin along with a seed as a reagent. When the recipe is satisfied, the finished item rises from the water.
Craft the Apothecary from any $(thing)stone$() in the shape of a pedestal and bowl — no Living Rock required.
mam.configuration.title: Might And Magic Configs
mam.ponder.pure_daisy.converts_stone.tex: Place the Pure Daisy near any Stone…
…and it slowly transmutes nearby Stone into Living Rock.
mam.ponder.pure_daisy.converts_log.text_: Oak Logs placed nearby are transmuted too…
…becoming Livingwood Logs, the foundation of verdant crafting.
mam.ponder.solarbud.sunlight.text_1: The Solarbud passively absorbs sunlight during the day, as long as it can see the sky…
mam.ponder.solarbud.sunlight.text_2: …slowly filling any Mana Pool within 6 blocks.
mam.ponder.emberwort.burning_fuel.text_1: Drop any furnace fuel within 3 blocks of the Emberwort…
mam.ponder.emberwort.burning_fuel.text_2: …and it burns the fuel, converting it into mana for a nearby pool.
mam.ponder.dewpetal.rain_and_water.text_: The Dewpetal generates mana in the rain — or when placed adjacent to a water source.
A single adjacent water source provides constant generation without needing rain.
